Across the largest AI labs & AI infrastructure companies, there is a common component : a lakehouse that stores data for training & inference called Lance.
Lance allows companies to manipulate massive collections of files in the most efficient way possible for AI.
 
Five production deployments show how that architecture runs at frontier scale :
Exa stores 35pb in Lance tables across 100b semantic web pages with crawl-to-search latency under five minutes. Index lead Jan van der Vegt explained :
"These column backfills allow us to keep the old data in place & only write what is new."
Runway runs Lance & LanceDB Enterprise across its video-generation stack. CTO Kamil Sindi noted :
"We first started using the Lance format in 2024 because it was the only option that handled unstructured data, column appends, distributed reads & ad-hoc SQL all at once."
Microsoft AI runs LanceDB inside its own tenant & security boundary. Head of Data Platform Suqiang "Jack" Song shared :
"We rely on LanceDB as the data layer for training across billions of rows of image & code data, with distributed inference reading the format directly across thousands of nodes."
Adobe manages 40pb to 50pb across 800k tables & 220b daily events, contributing 20+ pull requests upstream. As Adobe's platform team put it :
"Where should the AI-native data live? Our answer is in the same lakehouse, under the same contract as everything else."
NVIDIA closed the loop on physical AI. Cosmos tech lead Max Li explained :
"First ever, we train on thousands & tens of thousands of GPUs at scale with Lance tables directly."
Since its Series A last June, LanceDB has grown revenue more than 10x year over year across Netflix, Microsoft AI, Runway, Luma AI & Midjourney, while open-source downloads grew 6x past 120m.
Theory partnered with Chang She & Lei Xu at Seed & led their $30m Series A. Today we are thrilled to join Bessemer Venture Partners & Innovation Endeavors, alongside Dimension, Swift Ventures, CRV & Y Combinator, in LanceDB's $57.5m Series B.
Learn more about how to use Lance here.
Originally published on tomtunguz.com.

Check in daily. The newest in AI lives here: http://inspirationworld.ai  AI Inspiration World
New Models & Major Updates
1. Alibaba officially launches Qwen4-Max: a 2.4-trillion-parameter flagship, ~25% cheaper than its predecessor
Alibaba officially launched Qwen4-Max on November 16, the first flagship of the Qwen4 family: a new MoE architecture with 2.4 trillion total parameters and only 71 billion activated per token, native vision, and a 1-million-token context window. QwenCloud's pay-as-you-go API is priced at $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens — about 25% cheaper than Qwen3.8-Max. Alibaba says task costs are roughly 60% lower than the previous generation on its in-house Work360 benchmark (real tasks across 721 specialized fields; vendor-reported figures). The model is live on QwenCloud, Qwen Studio, QwenWork, and Qoder, and Alibaba says smaller Qwen4 models will be released as open weights, with no date given. This is the full launch five days after the November 11 preview, and a direct challenge from a Chinese lab to the flagship models from Anthropic and OpenAI. Source: PYMNTS
2. Tencent launches Hy4 flash: a 1M-context budget tier at just $0.07 per million input tokens
Tencent launched Hy4 flash on November 16, the cheaper sibling of Hy4 (released November 4): a 1-million-token context window with image understanding and tool calling, priced at $0.07 per million input tokens, $0.281 per million output tokens, and $0.003 per million cached input tokens. Hy4 flash is now listed in Tencent Cloud's model docs and API guide, supporting OpenAI Chat Completions, Responses, and Anthropic Messages protocols. With a "flagship + budget tier" two-layer pricing strategy, Tencent is extending the price war to the flagship tier itself — landing on the same day as Alibaba's Qwen4-Max launch. Source: CASRAI (citing TechNode and Tencent Cloud docs)
3. NVIDIA unveils Nemotron for Science at SC26: an open science-agent suite with a 50,000-question chemistry benchmark
NVIDIA introduced NVIDIA Nemotron for Science on November 16 at the SC26 supercomputing conference, built around the open Nemotron 3.5 Super VL model, plus a new open chemistry dataset, the LitmusBench v0.2 evaluation set (nearly 50,000 questions for training and evaluating chemistry reasoning), and post-training recipes to help research institutions build specialized science agents. The U.S. Department of Energy's Argonne National Laboratory is already using it to build research agents, and life-sciences companies including Lila Sciences and Terray Therapeutics are customizing the model. The model and dataset are available now on Hugging Face and can run locally on a 128GB NVIDIA DGX Spark system. This is NVIDIA's move from general-purpose assistants into "research assistants" — science agents are becoming the next battleground for model makers. Source: Morningstar (GlobeNewswire release)
Founders & Key Voices
1. Altman speaks publicly about Huang's exit for the first time: the AI industry "will be fine" without him, but it's "hard to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen"
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman spoke publicly for the first time about NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's resignation last week at Semafor's Silicon Valley & the World event on November 16. He called Huang a longtime personal hero, said it is "hard to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen," expressed "extreme gratitude" for NVIDIA's early bet on OpenAI, and said he has "strong personal empathy" for Huang's situation — drawing a parallel with his own 2023 ouster from OpenAI's board. But asked directly whether Huang should be reinstated, he declined to endorse a return, saying "I don't think I know enough to answer that question," while insisting that "there's so much demand, and it's so clear that AI is real, and revenues and demand are growing so strongly that I think the industry will be fine." He also said OpenAI "will go public at some point," because the world as a whole deserves exposure to the technology. Notably, NVIDIA's board has ruled out reinstating Huang while an internal probe continues, while Elon Musk and other executives have publicly called for his return. Source: Wccftech
Future AI Trends & Predictions
1. Altman warns AI chip demand is being "double counted" — a compute glut is coming, and someone will get burned
At the same Semafor event on November 16, Altman explained his warning to Samsung executives on October 31: many chipmakers now plan as if OpenAI, Anthropic, and a few others will absorb most of their output, so the same demand gets counted multiple times across vendors — meaning supply shocks and instability in the short term, and at some point a compute glut in which some players "get burned on infrastructure contracts." His view is that AI demand will still grow enormously in the long run, but short-term volatility is unavoidable. It is a rare public cold shower for the compute arms race from a frontier-lab CEO — and on the very same day, OpenAI signed a 457MW AMD compute deal (see Industry Dynamics), locking in more capacity even while warning of oversupply, which shows just how complicated this game is. Source: ReadModelMag (citing the Semafor event and Korean press reports)
Key Industry Moves
1. The Information: OpenAI explored a $5B+ acquisition of interpretability lab Goodfire — no deal done
The Information reported on November 16 that OpenAI leaders, including Sam Altman, held multiple talks over the summer about acquiring or partnering with Goodfire, a mechanistic interpretability startup, at a price above $5 billion — more than four times Goodfire's $1.25 billion valuation after its $150 million Series B in February. No deal or partnership emerged; Goodfire's leadership preferred to remain independent and sell its services to multiple AI developers. Goodfire works on reverse-engineering a model's internal computations to understand why it behaves the way it does, and Anthropic is a shareholder (a $1 million check it described as its first direct investment in another startup). The unconsummated deal shows OpenAI treats "understanding why a model thinks what it thinks" as a strategic asset on par with model capability itself. Source: Seeking Alpha (citing The Information)
2. TensorWave signs a six-year deal with OpenAI: 457MW of AMD compute, first capacity online in H1 2027
AI cloud provider TensorWave announced on November 16 a six-year agreement to supply OpenAI with 457 megawatts of dedicated IT capacity across multiple U.S. data center sites, powered by AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs in Helios rack-scale systems as dedicated single-tenant capacity for OpenAI. The first capacity is expected to come online in the first half of 2027, with full deployment by early 2028; financial terms were not disclosed. It is the first publicly announced neocloud supply deal under the OpenAI–AMD strategic partnership announced in October 2025 (covering 6GW of AMD chips), and a landmark win for the AMD camp in a compute market dominated by NVIDIA. Source: Business Wire (TensorWave announcement)
3. Amazon sells data centers to Blackstone in a $5B deal; AWS leases them back for 12+ years
Bloomberg reported on November 16 that Blackstone's data-center acquisition vehicle, Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BXDC), acquired a majority interest in two joint ventures with AWS in a $5 billion deal, covering 13 newly built powered shells across two data-center campuses in Indiana and Mississippi. BXDC will own 75% and AWS will retain 25%, leasing back the portfolio on an initial 12-year term extendable to 32 years. It is a new playbook for hyperscalers: monetize data-center real estate and lease it back, while Blackstone builds its data-center portfolio toward roughly $200 billion, aiming to become one of the biggest backers of AI infrastructure. Source: PYMNTS (citing Bloomberg)
4. EU hosts Apply AI Summit: a €10M call for a European media AI platform, deadline February 2027
The European Commission hosted the Apply AI Summit in Brussels on November 16–17, with about 900 people attending in person and thousands joining online, marking one year of the EU's Apply AI Strategy. A highlight was a new €10 million Horizon Europe call to build an interoperable, modular, multilingual AI media platform for European news and audiovisual organizations, designed to safeguard media pluralism and technological sovereignty. The call opened October 20, 2026 and closes February 16, 2027; selected proposals will enter grant negotiations in summer 2027, with deployment starting in autumn 2027. It is a step by the EU from AI regulation toward investing in public-interest AI infrastructure. Source: CASRAI (citing the European Commission)
